title: The Human Endocrine System
text: The endocrine system is the collection of glands that produce hormones, which are chemical messengers secreted into the bloodstream to regulate various bodily functions. Major endocrine glands include the pituitary (master gland), thyroid (metabolism), parathyroid (calcium regulation), adrenal (stress response via cortisol and adrenaline), pancreas (blood sugar via insulin and glucagon), and gonads (sex hormones). The hypothalamus links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland. Hormonal imbalances cause diseases such as diabetes (insulin deficiency or resistance), hypothyroidism, and Cushing's syndrome. The study of the endocrine system is called endocrinology.
